readerTitle: Why selling a year up front can quietly cost you
caseNote: 가상 사례 (동네 반려동물 용품점의 사료 정기배송, 물리치료 클리닉용 예약 소프트웨어) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 연간 결제 할인은 대개 어차피 남을 충성 고객에게 돌아간다. 그 대가로 얻는 것은 현금과 약정이고, 잃는 것은 매달 들어오던 고객 신호다.
misconception: 연간 선결제는 현금이 먼저 들어오고 이탈이 줄어드니 언제나 월 결제보다 낫다.

sources.text: 구독 결제 주기(연간·월간)에 대한 일반적인 경영 원리 (자기 선택, 선수금, 갱신 시점 집중)

factChecks.note: 계산 확인: 연간 플랜 $30 × 10개월 = $300(두 달 무료). 60명 × $300 = $18,000. 같은 60명이 월 결제로 1년 유지 시 60 × $30 × 12 = $21,600. 차이 $3,600. 연간 고객이 모두 1년 내내 남았을 것이라는 가정은 설명용입니다.
소프트웨어 사례(월 $100, 연간 40% 할인)는 가상 수치입니다. 실제 업계 평균 할인율이나 이탈률은 인용하지 않았습니다.
선수금(prepaid revenue)은 회계상 서비스 제공 전까지 수익이 아니라는 점은 일반 원리로만 서술했고, 특정 국가의 회계·세무 기준은 다루지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Sixty customers paid a year in advance. It cost the shop $3,600.
body: A neighborhood pet supply shop started delivering dog food for $30 a month. Then it offered an annual plan: pay $300 up front and get two months free.
Sixty of its 100 subscribers took the deal. The owner celebrated the cash in the bank. The cash was real. So was the cost.

image.label: Pet shop counter with a stack of cash and a calendar
image.brief: 따뜻한 일러스트. 작은 반려동물 용품점 계산대 위에 현금 더미와 12개월 달력. 달력의 마지막 달에만 빨간 동그라미. 사료 포대가 뒤에 쌓여 있음. 실제 브랜드 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Who takes the annual plan?
body: Before you see the numbers: which customers do you think chose to pay a full year up front?

options.text: Hesitant customers who wanted a discount to try it out
options.feedback: People who aren't sure they'll stay rarely commit to 12 months. The discount mostly never reaches them.

options.text: The most loyal customers, who were going to stay anyway
options.feedback: Right. Only confident customers prepay, so the discount went to people who would likely have paid full price.

options.text: A fairly random mix of customers
options.feedback: There's some mix, but people pick a plan based on how sure they are. The choice sorts them, so it isn't random.

cards.title: Follow the sixty.

breakdown.label: Discount given away
breakdown.detail: Paid to people who'd have stayed

cards.callout: The annual buyers had ordered for years. They also all reached renewal in the same month.

cards.title: Annual vs monthly billing
body: **Monthly billing** lets customers leave at any time. You collect less up front, but every month each customer quietly votes on whether you're still worth it.
**Annual billing** asks for a year's payment now, usually in exchange for a discount. You get cash and commitment. You pay with the discount, and you swap twelve small votes for one big one.
Neither is better. Each buys something different.

cards.title: The plan choice sorts your customers.
body: When you offer both, customers pick for themselves:
list: **Sure customers pick annual,** so the discount reaches people who'd stay anyway
**Unsure customers pick monthly,** so their cancellations stay visible
**Unhappy annual customers stay silent** until renewal
**Renewal month bunches up churn** into one big moment
cards.callout: An annual discount is a price cut for your best customers. Make sure you get something back.
cards.softwareNote: In software, annual plans often come with a month or two free. Check that against your real monthly churn: if few users leave anyway, the discount buys very little commitment.

cards.title: Sometimes the cash does real work.
body: Annual billing earns its discount when the cash or the commitment matters. A distributor that must buy a season's stock in advance can fund it with prepaid orders. A lawn treatment program that takes months to show results keeps customers through the slow start.
Monthly billing earns its place when the offer is new. Each cancellation is a lesson that arrives in time to act on it.

image.label: Scale weighing cash now against monthly feedback
image.brief: 저울 인포그래픽. 왼쪽 접시에 "Cash up front + commitment" 라벨의 동전 더미, 오른쪽 접시에 "Price + monthly feedback" 라벨의 작은 말풍선 12개. 저울은 수평에 가깝게.

cards.title: Prepaid cash isn't earned yet.
body: Annual money arrives before you deliver. Spend it like profit and month nine can get tight, with deliveries still owed. Refund requests also hurt more when they cover a whole year.
Prices get locked, too. If the shop's supplier raised dog food prices mid-year, every annual customer would still pay the old rate until renewal.

cards.title: Now it's booking software for clinics.
body: Your six-month-old startup sells appointment booking to small physio clinics for $100 a month. You're still fixing features clinics ask for. An adviser says to push everyone onto annual plans at 40% off for the cash.

options.text: Do it: more cash now and fewer cancellations
options.feedback: You'd cut price 40% for your keenest clinics and lose the monthly churn signal that shows what's broken while you can still fix it.

options.text: Keep monthly as the default and offer annual at a modest discount
options.feedback: You keep learning from monthly users while confident clinics lock in, without giving much away.

options.text: Offer monthly only, with no annual plan
options.feedback: The feedback stays clean, but you turn away cash and commitment some clinics would gladly give you.

cards.title: An annual plan is a trade, not a win.
body: You buy cash and commitment with a discount and with less feedback. Choose the plan that buys what you need most right now.
**Try it today:** list your prepaid or annual customers. How many would have stayed all year anyway? That's who your discount is paying.
